text:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-priority swap (v2 rollout) the 4-bit NF4 pool is showing a sustained throughput drop on prod-dedicated. p95 latency jumped and GPUs saw a memory bump. Anyone else seeing this?

jason: yep noticed around 03:20 UTC, traffic routing shows more requests hitting the nf4-optimized kernels. throughput down ~22% on the pool.

kevin: quick numbers from the perf dashboard: baseline throughput 9.8k tok/s -> 7.6k tok/s on the affected scheduler group. p50 latency 12ms -> 17.8ms. GPU mem +1.9GB on average for heads with >1024 seq.

lina: did the rollout change batching heuristics or KV cache affinity? those often surface when kernels swap priority.

maria: rollout was only kernel priority reorder: prioritized smaller-mem 4-bit matmul kernels over the fallback larger-kernels to reduce tail latency. No batching config changed in the release.

jason: repro on staging by forcing kernel-prio-swap with rwctl:
```bash
rwctl runtime update --group nf4-prod --swap-kernel-prio /configs/prio-v2.json
# then run the synthetic load job
rwctl job run --profile synth-4b-1024 --duration 5m
```
Observed same throughput drop locally.

kevin: profiler snippet attached (summarized):
```
kernel_select: matmul_4bit_fast      43% cycles
kernel_select: matmul_4bit_stable    28% cycles
batching_overhead: continuous_batch  12% cycles
kv_cache_lookup:                       7% cycles
mem_copy_async:                       10% cycles (spike)
```
Seems the "fast" kernel is increasing mem copies and stalls on big seq lengths.

lina: could be that the fast kernel has worse async mem behavior for >1k seq; at small seq it's great. We didn't account for seq distribution shift in the priority heuristic.

maria: what about calibration? We recently applied a NF4 quant calibration profile for v2 that changes block sizes — maybe interacts with kernel tile selection.

jason: good call. I pulled the calibration diffs: the new profile uses 16x4 blocks vs old 8x8 for some layers. That changes GEMM tiling patterns and could push certain codepaths into less-optimal assembler kernels.

kevin: quick mitigation: disable kernel-prio-swap for pools serving >30% long-context requests and fall back to previous kernel ordering. That should restore throughput while we root-cause.

lina: agreed. Also recommend adding a heuristic: when avg_seq > 768 prefer stable/kernel with lower async mem. I can PR the change to scheduler heuristics.

maria: +1 on revert for prod. Can someone open the rollback? @devops-bot any chance you can trigger the rollback for nf4-prod?

devops-bot: rollback job queued: job_id=rw-rollback-1805-01, targeting group=nf4-prod, action=restore-prio-v1. ETA 4m. :white_check_mark:

jason: after rolling back, metric snapshot shows throughput back to 9.7k tok/s and p50 ~12.3ms. GPU mem spike gone.

kevin: next steps:
- lina to add seq-aware heuristic + unit tests for tiling variants
- jason to add a microbenchmark that exercises both 8x8 and 16x4 calibration tiles across seq lengths 64/512/1024/2048
- maria to coordinate a staged canary after heuristic merge (small traffic first)

lina: I'll add the heuristic and also emit telemetry tagging kernels with calibration tile metadata so we can correlate in the console.

maria: for the microbench, include KV cache warm vs cold scenarios. We saw mem copy increases tied to cache miss churn in the profiler.

jason: already added synth test cases for KV warm/cold in the job above. Will expand to cover hot-kv-high-batch and cold-kv-high-batch.

kevin: also flag for QA: quality regression checks for NF4 changes — ensure generation metrics (perplexity + eval prompts) unchanged before re-enabling priority swap.

maria: agreed. I'll create the rollout ticket and link tests + metric thresholds. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4721

sre-ops: FYI I added an alert that triggers if throughput drops >15% for 5m after a scheduler change. Might reduce blast radius next time.

lina: one more thought — for long-term we should consider kernel-selection ML model that predicts best kernel per-layer/seq combo instead of global prio lists. But that's a bigger effort.

maria: noted. For now let's close the loop on the rollback and the seq-aware heuristic. thanks all :thumbsup:

jason: closing thread when ticket INF-4721 has test and heuristic PRs merged.

kevin: thanks — I'll monitor overnight and post a short postmortem if we see any re-occurrence.

maria: (closing)
